newsitem.title: USA: Compaq cuts U.S. prices on Notebook PCs. [CORRECTED 23:25 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Compaq cuts U.S. prices on Notebook PCs. [CORRECTED 23:25 GMT]

text.p: Compaq Computer Corp., the world's largest supplier of personal computers, Monday cut U.S. prices for its notebook PCs by as much as 20 percent.

The Houston-based company said prices for the computers will now start at $2,399 for on its LTE 5150 computer. Its highest-priced model, the LTE 5400, will now sell for $4,399 (corrects price from $5,199), a 15 percent reduction in price.
In February, the firm said it would lower U.S. prices on its desktops, portables, servers, workstation and networking products in an attempt to increase its market share among business customers.
Compaq's stock rose $1.875 to $81.125 early on the New York Stock Exchange.
